name: c-the-only-still-thing
prompt: Tall antique silver-gelatin photograph printed from a cracked glass plate, shot by a big wooden view camera locked off at seated eye height, square-on to a cast-iron park bench with wooden slats that sits across the bottom half of the frame, deep focus from front to back. One man occupies the middle of the bench, perfectly frontal, full figure from hat to boots: enormously fat, wealthy, in a tall gleaming stovepipe hat, a frock coat straining over a waistcoat, a gold watch chain looped across his belly, gloved hands, polished spats. His right hand is raised beside his shoulder, palm out, mid-dismissal. He alone is razor sharp, every stitch and whisker crisp, with a wide, calm, unmoving smile and pale eyes that hold the lens without blinking. The plate was left open on a bright overcast day for so long that everyone who came and went has dissolved into translucent drifts of grey: ranks of marching soldiers, a man on a crutch, nurses in scrubs, shoppers, a pram, whirling leaves, layer upon layer of half-erased bodies streaming past and even sitting beside him, faint as fog on a window, none casting a shadow. Only the fat man casts one, a solid black blot under the seat. Tonal range runs from soot black to cold paper white with no colour. The plate itself is decaying: a bluish metallic silvering creeping in from the borders, thin scratches, dust specks, one corner broken off to clear glass, a spidery crack across a lower edge. The top third is an almost blank, blown-out pale sky with a couple of bare twig tips, kept clear. Unsettling through stillness, never gore. No writing, signage or letters. Thanks.
